research_question: With a fixed scorer and the same 64 proposals, can a generator learned toward high-quality, accurately scored conditional target distributions reduce selection regret?

preregistered_promotion.primary: C minus B selected PDMS has a positive paired recording-bootstrap 95% lower bound on the locked development panel
preregistered_promotion.oracle_coverage: C minus A oracle-best PDMS is at least -1 point
preregistered_promotion.safety: C does not add any selected NC or DAC failure relative to A on this 64-scene pilot
preregistered_promotion.scope: Passing permits replication, not full-scale training or independent final-test claims

controls: A is the unmodified public DrivoR generator/scorer.
B/C update only copies of the same native final trajectory head, with identical initialization, batches, steps, optimizer and preservation losses.
B targets actual-quality-weighted native candidates; C adds measured scoring-error weighting with a target-quality guard.
Backbone, ego encoder, queries, trajectory decoder and scorer remain frozen and eval. No encoder forward during cached learning.
Training/tuning use disjoint recording groups within official NAVTRAIN. Official NAVVAL is not used as an independent split for this trainval-pretrained checkpoint.
NAVTEST64 is the previously exposed development panel; no NAVTEST targets enter teacher construction, gradient updates or checkpoint selection.
All modified candidates are rescored as a full64 set and reevaluated with official PDMS; original labels are never reused for changed coordinates.
Final comparison is fixed step300 for both learned conditions, not a test-selected checkpoint.
No full-scale extension, CEM, new scorer adaptation or backbone training is automatically launched.
